Pea fruit from polluted sites in Egypt carried far more cadmium and lead than fruit from unpolluted sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span </li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Compare cadmium with the EU maximum of 100 µg/kg for proteins from pulses, not the 40 µg/kg row for pulses.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ask for lot results that name the form, the basis and a quantification limit well below that maximum.

<a id="pea-protein-overview"></a>
<a id="decision-summary"></a>
## Pea protein overview

<a id="hmi-ing-004"></a>
<a id="which-contamination-concerns-are-supported-for-this-ingredient-and-its-defined-forms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-005"></a>
<a id="which-sourcing-or-production-decisions-deserve-priority-on-the-available-evidence"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-006"></a>
<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Pea protein on this page is the powdered protein fraction of field pea, sold as an isolate, a concentrate, or a retail powder. Whole peas and multi-ingredient blends are discussed only where a study measured them, and they are not pooled with the isolate. Two retail pea powders bought online and in Cork, Ireland, in 2016 and 2017 contained 40.6 and 15.4 µg/kg cadmium and 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg lead, as sold.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Total mercury in those two powders was 4.3 µg/kg and below 0.2 µg/kg, total chromium was 289.2 and 210.7 µg/kg, and total tin was 26.7 and 329.7 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Two anonymized commercial pea concentrates, each bought twice, showed nickel means of 585.49 and 268.27 µg/kg and total chromium means of 78.97 and 114.11 µg/kg, with cadmium and lead not detected.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The European cadmium maximum that names proteins from pulses is 100 µg/kg, set beside 40 µg/kg for pulses other than that protein row.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For a buyer the first distinction is the material: isolate or concentrate versus whole seed, frozen peas, or a blend. The second is the basis, because a dry-weight fruit result and an as-sold powder result are not the same measurement. The third is the reporting limit, because a non-detect is an interval up to that limit and not a measured zero. The Irish powders and the Spanish concentrates do not record the country where the peas were grown, so they cannot rank Canada, China, or the European Union as growing origins.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lot testing describes the lot in hand, and it does not remove cadmium, lead, or any other element from the powder.



<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers pea protein as a food ingredient: the protein-rich powder made from field pea, including isolates and concentrates sold as such. The Irish evidence is two retail products the authors classified as pea, among 36 protein powders that also included whey, soy, casein, and mixed plant powders.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The concentrate evidence is two anonymized commercial pea protein concentrates, bought from online shops and analyzed beside rice and soybean concentrates in the same paper.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third form in the table is garden pea fruit, oven-dried, from farms in South Cairo and Giza, which is the pea pod's seed tissue as a vegetable and not a separated protein.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Frozen boiled green peas in the US Total Diet Study, and Canadian field pea seed in a 2009 grain baseline, are cited as other materials and are not rows of this powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

An isolate is a higher-protein powder than a concentrate, but these studies do not print a protein percentage for the packages they tested, so the page keeps the authors' own names. A retail powder can also contain flavor, sweetener, or another protein, and the Irish paper identifies the two pea products as pea rather than as a named blend.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Plant powders that list pea together with rice or seeds are blends, and a metal in the blend cannot be assigned to the pea fraction. Dry-weight, as-sold, and unstated results stay in separate comparisons, and this page does not apply a moisture conversion. Transferring a whole-pea concentration onto an isolate, or an isolate concentration onto frozen peas, would treat different foods as one food.

## Heavy metal contamination profile of pea protein

<a id="which-metals-and-chemical-species-have-been-investigated-in-this-ingredient"></a>

The table lists every extracted result for this page: the Irish pea powders, the two pea concentrates, and the Egyptian garden pea fruit means. On the Irish powders as sold, cadmium was 40.6 µg/kg in one package and 15.4 µg/kg in the other, and lead was 22.2 and 22.5 µg/kg.<sup Few of these powder rows can be rated against an HMI reference, because a reference needs at least four compatible medians or sample values for the same form and basis, and the method sentence is not repeated under every metal.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-pea-protein-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of pea protein, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Pea protein, powder or ground; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>22.2</td><td>22.4</td><td>22.5</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>22.2</td><td>22.4</td><td>22.5</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>2 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Ring et al. 2021</td><td>2</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for pea protein, powder or ground on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>Ring et al. 2021 is the only compatible sampling family for pea protein, powder or ground on this basis in the completed pea protein ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Ring et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-11-03. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-9abd3cdd6591:fd8bde5fc313</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-f78a9cb8a2a4:4e957c08e0ec"><summary>HMI pea protein Cd reference · Pea protein, powder or ground</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:pea-protein-f78a9cb8a2a4:4e957c08e0ec"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI pea protein Cd reference · Pea protein, powder or ground. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

Cadmium and lead reach peas from the soil and from dust or waste deposited on the crop, and the element remains in the tissue because cooking and drying do not destroy it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A review by FDA scientists describes diet as the main cadmium exposure for people who are not exposed at work and do not smoke, and it identifies soil pH, cultivar, and fertilizer choice as levers on how much the plant takes up.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> That review's highest mean foods in the US Total Diet Study were not peas, which is a reminder that a concentrated protein ingredient and a boiled vegetable are different exposure questions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Field pea is a pulse, and pulses are known to take cadmium up from soil, but the size of that uptake is a property of the soil, the variety, and the season, not a single concentration for every origin. No powder study in this library paired the metal in the seed with the metal in the isolate made from that seed, so the pathway into the powder is inferred from the crop and from the process, not measured end to end.

The direct crop comparison on this page is garden pea grown in South Cairo and Giza in the winter of 2017.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Fruit from farms that received waste from cement, iron and steel, brick, and fertilizer works contained much more lead, cadmium, chromium, and nickel than fruit from the study's unpolluted farms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The unpolluted fruit was not a clean commercial baseline either: 2.6 mg/kg cadmium and 8.9 mg/kg lead, dry weight, are far above the Irish retail powders.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The authors report bioaccumulation factors above 1 for several metals at the polluted sites, which means the plant tissues held more metal than the soil measurement they used, but that factor is for those sites and not a universal pea constant.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Industrial fruit and a retail isolate answer different questions, and the fruit series is here to show how strongly site can move the crop, not to describe protein sold for food manufacture.

and 22.5 µg/kg, while whey lead ran from 0.8 to 88.4 µg/kg and one mixed plant powder was 49.5 µg/kg, so the highest lead package in that study was whey.<sup A Canada, China, and European Union ranking of pea protein isolate is not supported by the measurements in hand. The Canadian Grain Commission baseline of field pea seed reports, in its abstract, a mean cadmium of 0.023 mg/kg, with arsenic and lead below 0.050 mg/kg and mercury below 0.002 mg/kg, and the full sample table was not available.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> That abstract describes whole seed, not an isolate, and it does not give the number of samples or the years, so it is not an occurrence row and not a sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No eligible study here measured pea protein isolate grown in China, or separated European-grown isolate from European retail of unknown origin. Until origin is printed with the lot, the lowest observed package in one shop is only the lowest package in that shop.


<a id="processing-cooking-and-preparation"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Separating protein from pea removes starch and fiber and dries what remains, which can raise the metal concentration per kilogram if the metal stays with the protein and the discarded fraction held less. That is a mass-balance expectation, not a result from these papers, because none of them analyzed the seed, the isolate, and the side streams from the same lot. The European cadmium table is the regulatory trace of that expectation: pulses other than proteins from pulses are 0.040 mg/kg, and proteins from pulses are 0.10 mg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The protein maximum is 2.5 times the pulse maximum, which is legal room for a more concentrated ingredient, not a measured yield from a factory trial. The Irish pea powders at 15.4 and 40.6 µg/kg cadmium sit under the 100 µg/kg protein row, and that comparison is two packages, not a compliance rate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Wet fractionation, which solubilizes protein and then precipitates it, and dry fractionation, which separates by air classification, can move minerals differently, and this library does not contain a head-to-head metal balance for pea. Heat does not destroy lead, cadmium, arsenic, or mercury, so roasting or cooking changes a concentration only by moving water or by parting a fraction that carries the metal.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Drying a wet vegetable raises the concentration per kilogram without adding metal, which is one reason a dry powder and a boiled pea are not compared by the raw number. The Egyptian fruit was oven-dried before analysis, so its milligrams per kilogram are dry weight and would look lower on a fresh pea that is mostly water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A process claim that an isolate step removes cadmium needs the before and after on the same lot, with the basis and the yield stated, and that pair is not in these studies.


<a id="mitigation-for-pea-protein"></a>
<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for pea protein

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

No study in this library measured a treatment that lowered lead, cadmium, arsenic, or mercury in pea protein and reported the size of that change. The crop literature points upstream: soil pH, cultivar, and fertilizer choice change how much cadmium a plant takes up, which is the step that keeps the metal out of the seed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Those levers were not tested on the retail powders or the concentrates reviewed here, so they are a research direction and not a quantified benefit for this ingredient.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Egyptian contrast shows the other side of siting, because fruit beside cement, iron, and fertilizer works held far more metal than the study's other farms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Choosing a growing area away from that kind of waste is supported as a difference in that study, and it is not a universal map of clean regions for protein isolate.

Once the powder is made, the verifiable control in this evidence is lot testing against the maximum that applies to the legal category of the product. A specification sheet that repeats a target, without a method and a result for the lot, does not show what the lot contains. Washing or cooking advice drawn from vegetables does not transfer to a dry protein powder that has already been milled and dried. Blending pea with a lower-metal protein would change the blend, and it would not change the pea fraction, and this page does not have a measured dilution trial. The absence of a measured removal step is recorded as a gap, not as evidence that no control exists in the factory.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No study in this library has yet measured a way to lower heavy metals in pea protein; the studies here compare contaminated and ordinary growing settings, and lot testing against the applicable limit remains the verifiable check.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that is lower in lead can be higher in cadmium, nickel, or chromium. In the Irish set the highest lead powder was whey, while the highest cadmium powders were mixed plant, and the pea powders were mid-pack for lead and higher than most whey for cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In the concentrate set, pea was the lower total chromium pair and not a lower nickel pair, and one rice concentrate carried detected lead while the pea concentrates did not.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A blend that looks low in one metal can still carry another metal from rice, cocoa, or a flavor ingredient, and the pea share of that blend is not identified. Avoiding an industrial waste site lowered fruit metals in one Egyptian study, and that choice is not a measured cost, yield, or protein-quality result.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

The powders in the Irish study were microwave-digested and measured by sector-field inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, with results reported per kilogram of powder as sold.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The concentrates were microwave-digested in nitric acid and measured by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry, and the paper does not state a dry-weight or as-sold basis for the mineral block.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A lot report that a buyer can use names the form, the basis, the analyte, the method, the result, and the quantification limit. For a 100 µg/kg cadmium maximum, a quantification limit of a few micrograms per kilogram can show the distance to the maximum, and a limit of 200 µg/kg cannot.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Total chromium is not hexavalent chromium, and total arsenic is not inorganic arsenic, unless the method speciates them.

The concentrate footnotes print detection limits below 0.015 and below 0.026 under the ppb heading and do not repeat the unit, so this page does not treat 0.015 µg/kg as a demonstrated food limit of quantification.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Hungarian plant powders were below detection for arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and lead, and the paper does not print those detection limits, so the non-detect cannot be placed on a number line.<sup class="cite">[[sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Horváth IL, Kajner G, Galbács G, Csupor D · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/horvath2025-hungary-protein-powders-metals">Analysis of heavy metal content in protein powders available on the the product is a pea and rice blend, because rice is the ingredient that usually drives inorganic arsenic. A single composite or a single package is not a year's production, and the Irish design is one analysis per product.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Ask for the lot identity on the certificate, the digestion, the basis, and the limit of quantification, and do not accept a target copied from a sales specification as if it were a result.

href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A pea protein ingredient in a food is not automatically a food supplement, so the buyer has to know which legal category the lot is placed on the market under. Nickel maxima added in 2024 set 4.0 mg/kg for pulses except dry beans and dry lupins, applying from 1 July 2025, and there is no separate nickel row for proteins from pulses.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Processed foods that are not themselves a listed category are handled by the concentration and dilution rules of the contaminants regulation, not by inventing a new number.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The nickel measured in the two pea concentrates, about 268 to 585 µg/kg, is numerically below 4,000 µg/kg, and that is not a compliance test, because the basis is unstated and the legal row is the pulse.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> This page did not verify a United States maximum written for pea protein or for proteins from pulses, and the Total Diet Study figures for boiled peas are monitoring results, not limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A purchasing specification should name lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic when rice is in the formula, total mercury, and nickel, each with a quantification limit below the maximum that applies. Origin language on a contract is only as good as the lot record that ties the powder to a harvest region, which these retail studies do not provide.

## Evidence review and remaining gaps

<a id="hmi-ing-034"></a>
<a id="which-primary-regulatory-instruments-apply-to-this-exact-ingredient-form-species-market-and-date"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-035"></a>
<a id="what-searches-eligibility-decisions-source-families-and-appraisal-underpin-the-answers-and-certainty-judgments"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-036"></a>
<a id="what-remains-unresolved-when-was-each-answer-reviewed-and-what-changed-in-this-version"></a>

The occurrence rows come from the Irish retail survey, the concentrate mineral table, and the Egyptian fruit table, each read for the pea material the paper actually measured. Plant-protein blends, a unit-unresolved survey of vegan powders, and an Indian labeling study that pooled pea with soy were not entered as pea protein concentrations, because the pea fraction or the unit could not be defended. Industry market reports that are not peer-reviewed and do not publish a concentration table were not used as numbers. Supplier notices and company certificates of analysis were excluded, including any notice written for a single manufacturer's pea protein. The 2009 Canadian field-pea article remains closed: the abstract means are cited with that limit, and they are not rows.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

What is still missing is a multi-lot survey of pea protein isolate with growing origin, basis, and quantification limits for lead, cadmium, inorganic arsenic, and total mercury. A paired seed and isolate from the same lots would show whether protein separation concentrates cadmium, which the legal 40 versus 100 µg/kg split only allows for and does not measure.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Two Irish packages and two concentrates are enough to show the ingredient is not free of these elements, and they are not enough for a rated reference or a regional ranking. The Egyptian fruit series is strong evidence about a polluted agricultural district and weak evidence about commercial protein. Corrections to a misread table, a retrieved Canadian full text, or a new origin-linked survey should reopen the affected paragraphs.

References identify the sources used in these answers. The Sources index preserves additional discovery links; inclusion there does not mean a source has been reviewed for this assessment. Corrections, completed searches, new direct evidence and changes in requirements should reopen the relevant answer.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-cadmium-and-lead-get-into-peas" data-anchor="how-do-cadmium-and-lead-get-into-peas" data-question="How do cadmium and lead get into peas?">

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The plant takes cadmium and lead up from soil, and contaminated dust or waste can add more, which is why site matters.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Soil pH, the variety, and the fertilizer program change uptake, according to a review of dietary cadmium by FDA scientists.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In South Cairo and Giza, pea fruit beside cement, iron, brick, and fertilizer works held 1,025 mg/kg cadmium and 121 mg/kg lead, dry weight.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" from the study's other farms held 2.6 mg/kg cadmium and 8.9 mg/kg lead, dry weight, which is lower than the polluted fruit and still high next to retail powders.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman
