</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-making-an-isolate-concentrate-the-metals" data-anchor="does-making-an-isolate-concentrate-the-metals" data-question="Does making an isolate concentrate the metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does making an isolate concentrate the metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Protein separation discards starch and fiber and dries the protein fraction, so a metal that follows the protein can be higher per kilogram in the powder than in the seed. No paper in this set measured the same lot as seed and as isolate, so that concentration is not a measured factor here. European law sets cadmium at 40 µg/kg for pulses and at 100 µg/kg for proteins from pulses, which leaves room for a more concentrated ingredient.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The Irish pea powders at 15.4 and 40.6 µg/kg cadmium are under the protein row, and two packages do not show how often that happens.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Heat does not destroy the elements, so a roasting step is not, by itself, a removal step.<sup class="cite">[[sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies|9]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Schaefer HR, Dennis S, Fitzpatrick S · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Cadmium: Mitigation strategies to reduce dietary exposure</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Food Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/schaefer2020-cadmium-mitigation-strategies">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-canadian-chinese-or-european-peas-lower" data-anchor="are-canadian-chinese-or-european-peas-lower" data-question="Are Canadian, Chinese, or European peas lower?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are Canadian, Chinese, or European peas lower?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

None of the powder studies records the country where the peas were grown, so Canada, China, and the European Union cannot be ranked as isolate origins. The Irish powders were bought in Ireland, and the concentrates were bought online for a laboratory in Spain.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A Canadian Grain Commission paper on field pea seed reports a mean cadmium of 0.023 mg/kg in its abstract, with arsenic and lead below 0.050 mg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The full article is closed, the sample table was not read, and the material is whole seed rather than isolate.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A sourcing preference needs origin on the lot, the same form, and the same basis, and those three are not together in this library.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-pea-powders-compare-with-whey-and-other-plant-powders" data-anchor="how-do-pea-powders-compare-with-whey-and-other-plant-powders" data-question="How do pea powders compare with whey and other plant powders?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do pea powders compare with whey and other plant powders?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the Irish survey the two pea powders were higher in cadmium than most of the 27 whey powders and lower than the two mixed plant powders.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Whey cadmium ran from below 0.61 to 23.2 µg/kg, pea was 15.4 and 40.6, and mixed plant was 45.1 and 58.1.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead did not follow cadmium: pea was about 22 µg/kg and the highest lead result was 88.4 µg/kg in a whey powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Among two pea and two rice concentrates, detected lead was in one rice product, and total chromium was higher in both rice products than in either pea product.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Two or four products are a comparison inside one study, not a ranking of the world's pea protein against the world's whey.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-legal-limits-apply" data-anchor="what-legal-limits-apply" data-question="What legal limits apply?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What legal limits apply?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Proteins from pulses have a European cadmium maximum of 0.10 mg/kg, and other pulses have 0.040 mg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Those rows were set in the 2021 cadmium amendment and are carried in the contaminants regulation now in force.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Food supplements have a cadmium maximum of 1.0 mg/kg as placed on the market, except the higher seaweed and bivalve supplement row.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Nickel in pulses except dry beans and lupins is 4.0 mg/kg from 1 July 2025, and that row is not written as proteins from pulses.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A processed food that is not a listed category uses the regulation's concentration rules rather than a blank cell or an invented number.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-should-a-laboratory-report-include" data-anchor="what-should-a-laboratory-report-include" data-question="What should a laboratory report include?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What should a laboratory report include?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The report should name the form, such as isolate, concentrate, or blend, and the basis, such as as sold or dry weight. It should list lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic if rice is in the product, total mercury, and nickel, each with its own result. The quantification limit should sit well below the maximum that applies, for example well below 100 µg/kg where the protein cadmium row applies.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Commission Regulation (EU) 2021/1323 of 10 August 2021 amending Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006 as regards maximum levels of cadmium in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 288, 11.8.2021, p. 13–18)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2021-1323-cadmium-foodstuffs-amendment">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The method should be an acid digestion and a mass-spectrometric or equivalent determination, with the lot identity on the same page.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A non-detect should show the limit, and a limit whose unit is not stated cannot be used as a food concentration.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-the-concentrate-non-detects-mean-the-cadmium-is-very-low" data-anchor="do-the-concentrate-non-detects-mean-the-cadmium-is-very-low" data-question="Do the concentrate non-detects mean the cadmium is very low?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do the concentrate non-detects mean the cadmium is very low?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The paper marks cadmium and lead as not detected in both pea concentrates.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The footnotes give limits below 0.015 and below 0.026 and do not restate whether that unit is the digest or the food.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A food limit of quantification near 0.02 µg/kg would be unusually low next to the Irish method, which reported cadmium down to below 0.61 µg/kg in a whey powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Until the unit is clear, the honest statement is that the concentrates did not report a detected cadmium or lead value. It is not a finding that those products sit at a fraction of a microgram per kilogram.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="was-arsenic-measured" data-anchor="was-arsenic-measured" data-question="Was arsenic measured?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Was arsenic measured?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Arsenic was not among the elements in the Irish protein-powder method.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The concentrate mineral table that includes nickel, chromium, cadmium, and lead does not include arsenic or mercury.<sup class="cite">[[sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rocio Lopez-Calabozo, Ivan Martinez-Martin, Marta Rodriguez-Fernandez, Yamina Absi, Ana Maria Vivar-Quintana, Isabel Revilla · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">The Influence of the Nutritional and Mineral Composition of Vegetable Protein Concentrates on Their Functional Properties</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Foods</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/lopezcalabozo2025-vegetable-protein-concentrates">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Garden pea fruit in Egypt was measured for total arsenic, at 0.03 mg/kg on unpolluted-site fruit and 0.1 mg/kg on polluted-site fruit, dry weight, without speciation.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Boiled frozen peas in the US Total Diet Study were not detected for total arsenic at a reporting limit of 3 µg/kg, which is the vegetable and not the powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> If a product also contains rice, inorganic arsenic has to be asked for separately, because these pea-only tables do not supply it.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="should-the-egyptian-pea-results-change-how-powders-are-read" data-anchor="should-the-egyptian-pea-results-change-how-powders-are-read" data-question="Should the Egyptian pea results change how powders are read?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Should the Egyptian pea results change how powders are read?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

They should change how the crop is understood, and they should not be pasted onto a protein specification. The polluted fruit is evidence that industrial waste near the field can push pea cadmium and lead into the hundreds or thousands of milligrams per kilogram, dry weight.<sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The unpolluted fruit in the same provinces was already 2.6 mg/kg cadmium, dry weight, which is not what the Irish retail powders showed.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Galal TM, Hassan LM, Ahmed DA, Alamri SAM, Alrumman SA, Eid EM · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Heavy metals uptake by the global economic crop (Pisum sativum L.) grown in contaminated soils and its associated health risks</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLoS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/galal2021-heavy-metals-pisum-sativum">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The table keeps that fruit as its own form so the powder rows stay readable beside it. A buyer of isolate should ask where the crop was grown and for a lot result, and should not treat either Egyptian mean as the expected powder concentration.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-frozen-peas-compare" data-anchor="how-do-frozen-peas-compare" data-question="How do frozen peas compare?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do frozen peas compare?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The US Total Diet Study measured frozen green peas after boiling, as the food is eaten.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Three composites showed cadmium in two, up to 3.2 µg/kg, with a reporting limit of 1 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead, total mercury, and total arsenic were not detected, at reporting limits of 4, 1, and 3 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Those figures are as consumed and water-rich, so they sit far below a dry protein on a per-kilogram basis for reasons of water as well as process. They belong on the frozen pea record as the vegetable, and they are cited here only to keep the powder from being confused with the vegetable.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-is-still-too-thin-to-settle" data-anchor="what-is-still-too-thin-to-settle" data-question="What is still too thin to settle?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What is still too thin to settle?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Two retail packages and two concentrates do not make a distribution, a percentile, or a pass rate for the ingredient. Growing origin is missing on the powders, and the Canadian seed baseline is an abstract without its table.<sup class="cite">[[sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Gawalko E, Garrett RG, Warkentin T, Wang N, Richter A · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Trace elements in Canadian field peas: a grain safety assurance perspective</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives and Contaminants: Part A</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/gawalko2009-canadian-field-peas-trace-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Inorganic arsenic and, for the concentrates, mercury were not measured. No before-and-after process trial shows how much metal the isolate step keeps. Those gaps are why the page states what was measured and does not offer a regional winner or a removal percentage.

</div>
</details>

## What remains uncertain

Arsenic was not measured in the retail powders or the concentrates, and the fruit arsenic result is total arsenic on dry garden pea, not inorganic arsenic in a powder.<sup class="cite">[[sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Ring G, Sheehan A, Lehane M, Furey A · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Development, Validation and Application of an ICP-SFMS Method for the Determination of Metals in Protein Powder Samples, Sourced in Ireland, with Risk Assessment for Irish Consumers</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2021, 26, 4347</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/ring2021-ireland-protein-powders-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup
